title: Dashboard
description: Monitor platform health, servers, projects, applications, and recent runs from a real-time overview.

sections.title: Platform indicators
sections.content: The cards summarize online and offline servers, pending tasks, and running pipelines. Application health distinguishes an available, degraded, unavailable, or unknown service.

sections.title: Servers and projects
sections.content: The lists show resources you can access. Open a server or project to enter its detail workspace. Capability diagnostics identify whether an agent can build, deploy, or manage a target.

sections.title: Monitored applications
sections.content: The Monitored applications area lists every tracked application, its availability, and its latest status change. Current visitors appear only when web analytics are available. Data refreshes in real time when application state changes.

sections.title: Recent activity
sections.content: Recent runs show project, pipeline, status, and update time. Open a run to inspect its definition, steps, logs, and results.

sections.title: Custom dashboard
sections.content: An administrator can replace the standard overview with a custom dashboard marked as default. Use **Manage dashboards** to create and arrange its widgets.

title: Servers and agents
description: Enroll agents, monitor compatibility, and manage the services and resources available on each machine.

sections.title: Server fleet
sections.content: Search by name, hostname, or tags; filter by type, status, and agent compatibility; and choose visible columns. Badges identify insecure TLS, deployment capability, and compatibility level. **Update all agents** starts a bulk operation for eligible agents.

sections.title: Add an agent
sections.content: The **Add agent** wizard creates a registration token and Linux or Windows instructions using the backend URL. Copy the command or all instructions, install the service on the target, and wait for its first heartbeat. Treat a registration token as a secret used only for enrollment.

sections.title: Presence and compatibility
sections.content: Heartbeats drive Online/Offline state and metrics. **Contact agent** checks recent presence and returns diagnostics. Up to date, Update recommended, Update required, and Unknown compare version, protocol, and expected capabilities. An update may wait for active tasks to finish.

sections.title: Overview and properties
sections.content: Overview shows CPU, memory, disk, uptime, heartbeat, and diagnostics. Properties and Configuration contain identity, tags, capabilities, runner options, container isolation, and TLS options. Edit and Delete require the appropriate permissions.

sections.title: Services and modules
sections.content: Services lets you select, install, start, stop, restart, or uninstall supported services. Docker, Apache, Certbot, Mail, TeamSpeak, Portsentry, and Rkhunter pages expose module-specific data and actions. Operations are blocked when the agent is offline or lacks the required capability.

sections.title: System administration
sections.content: Cron, Firewall, and Updates expose system operations allowed by the agent installation. Applications, Modules, and Services reflect collected inventory. Elevation is never implicit: only capabilities enabled during installation are offered.

sections.title: Linked resources
sections.content: Projects, Pipelines, Libraries, Vaults, Releases, Tasks, and Logs filter the resources linked to the server. They reuse the permissions, filters, and actions of their global views.

sections.title: Real-time and security
sections.content: Heartbeats, task states, and logs arrive in real time. Subscriptions are restored and data is reconciled after reconnect. Administrative actions remain subject to resource permissions and agent capabilities.

title: Projects
description: Organize repositories, pipelines, targets, quality, backups, and operations in a shared project workspace.

sections.title: List and views
sections.content: Search and filter projects by status, favorites, or sort order. Dense and comfortable modes adjust presentation. Cards can show the latest commit, run, production state, analysis grade, and users currently present.

sections.title: Create or edit
sections.content: Set the name, description, repository URL, default branch, and tags. A project belongs to an organization and its actions follow permissions. The Edit page centralizes these settings.

sections.title: Overview and board
sections.content: Overview combines status, README, Git information, pipelines, and activity. The board organizes project work into columns and movable items when that feature is configured.

sections.title: Delivery
sections.content: Pipelines, Releases, Artifacts, and Environments cover definition, execution, promotion, and deliverables. Servers associates available targets with the project.

sections.title: Shared configuration
sections.content: Libraries provide non-sensitive variables and Vaults provide encrypted secrets. Resources can be inherited according to owner scope and effective permissions.

sections.title: Quality, backups, and AI
sections.content: Quality opens the project analysis portfolio. Backups manages policies and restore checks. AI tasks runs definitions owned by the project with a selected runner profile.

sections.title: Operations
sections.content: Monitoring combines availability and telemetry. Tasks and Logs filter project activity. External repository exposes the source repository connection. Sections preserve project context and update from available events.

title: Git repositories
description: Manage project Git mirrors and explore code, branches, commits, tags, protection rules, and pull requests.

sections.title: Create and synchronize
sections.content: A repository belongs to a project and has a name, description, default branch, and status. The backend maintains a local mirror used for browsing and Git operations. Refresh to retrieve remote changes.

sections.title: Code and files
sections.content: Browse the tree, open files, copy content, and read the rendered README. Binary files are identified and are not rendered as text.

sections.title: Branches, tags, and commits
sections.content: Create a branch or tag, set the default branch, and inspect the commit graph. A commit view shows author, date, parents, changed files, and diff; first-parent mode clarifies merge commits.

sections.title: Blame and history
sections.content: Blame associates each line with a commit. Commit search and branch detail pages help investigate a specific change.

sections.title: Protection and pull requests
sections.content: Branch rules can require a pull request and prevent deletion or force-push. Pull requests expose source, target, status, and merge actions when your permissions allow them.

sections.title: Real-time and permissions
sections.content: Branch, tag, commit, and push changes arrive in real time. Create, delete, protect, and merge actions remain subject to repository and project permissions.

title: Environments
description: Define deployment targets, servers, approvals, and safety controls for dynamic analysis.

sections.title: Definition
sections.content: An environment belongs to a project and has a name, description, and type such as Development, Testing, Staging, or Production. Associate the servers that form the target.

sections.title: Approval
sections.content: Enable **Approval required** to pause deployment until a decision. Instructions describe what reviewers must check and the approval timeout limits waiting.

sections.title: DAST
sections.content: To allow dynamic analysis, enable DAST and explicitly state whether the environment is ephemeral and contains real data. Allowed hosts bound the targets the scanner may contact.

sections.title: Pipeline use
sections.content: A pipeline selects the environment to resolve servers and approval rules. The run page identifies the selected target and blocks an operation whose prerequisites are not satisfied.

title: Pipelines
description: Design, validate, and run traceable CI/CD workflows with logs, results, artifacts, quality, and deployment controls.

sections.title: Create a pipeline
sections.content: Choose project, server, or owner scope, then set name, description, source branch, and trigger. A pipeline can start blank, from a template, or from a Git-managed repository definition.

sections.title: YAML and visual editors
sections.content: YAML mode provides formatting and validation. Visual mode organizes stages, jobs, steps, dependencies, agent, operating system, and variables. Add, duplicate, move, or delete items while keeping the equivalent definition.

sections.title: Validation and dry run
sections.content: **Validate YAML** checks structure. Dry run prepares resolved commands without applying effects. Review the diff before saving to understand changes from the stored version.

sections.title: Variables, secrets, and connections
sections.content: Libraries provide non-sensitive values, Vaults provide masked secrets, and Service connections provide integration credentials. Template and run parameters complete these values at start time.

sections.title: Triggers
sections.content: A run can be manual, scheduled, webhook-driven, or started by another pipeline. Branch and commit are fixed for reproducibility. Environment approvals can pause progress.

sections.title: Run tracking
sections.content: Run detail shows status, progress, stages, steps, duration, commands, output, and logs. Follow and search logs, collapse command or output, copy logs, and jump to top or bottom.

sections.title: Cancel and rerun
sections.content: Cancel an active run. Rerun a completed run on the same commit, branch head, or failed steps when available. Lineage links parent and child runs.

sections.title: Results and deliverables
sections.content: Tabs combine tests, coverage by file or assembly, lint, complexity, artifacts, and release. Analysis gates show reports, new findings, blockers, warnings, and missing producers.

sections.title: Fleet and templates
sections.content: Fleet compares pipelines linked to a template, pinned version, and latest available version. It opens compatible updates and identifies legacy unpinned references.

sections.title: Real-time and access
sections.content: Progress, steps, logs, results, and completion arrive in real time and reconcile after reconnect. Available actions depend on pipeline, project, server, and environment permissions.

title: Pipeline templates
description: Version and reuse pipeline definitions with parameters, changelogs, and controlled updates.

sections.title: Catalog
sections.content: Search templates, filter by category, and inspect version, description, and use count. Create, edit, delete, import, or export according to your permissions.

sections.title: Create and use
sections.content: A template contains name, category, description, YAML definition, and changelog. **Use template** creates a pipeline and requests declared parameters.

sections.title: Extract from a pipeline
sections.content: Extraction converts an existing definition into a template, detects values to turn into parameters, and can rewrite the source pipeline to pin the created version.

sections.title: Publish a version
sections.content: Promotion compares the new definition, requests a changelog entry, and publishes an immutable version. The source pipeline can then be rebased onto it.

sections.title: History
sections.content: History shows versions, dates, authors, and changelog. A version used by a pipeline remains identifiable when a newer version exists.

sections.title: Update a pipeline
sections.content: Update shows the version transition and overrides. Orphaned overrides require explicit acknowledgement before confirmation to avoid silent configuration loss.

title: Variable libraries
description: Centralize reusable non-sensitive pipeline values with owner scopes, import, export, and history.

sections.title: Scope and inheritance
sections.content: A library belongs to an allowed scope, such as project, environment, or project-server. Global and contextual views identify inherited resources and their origin.

sections.title: Entries
sections.content: Add, edit, or remove key-value pairs. Keys become references in pipeline definitions; use stable naming to avoid collisions.

sections.title: Import and export
sections.content: Export a library for backup or transfer, then import a compatible file. Review keys before saving because an import can replace an existing key value.

sections.title: Versions
sections.content: History shows stored versions and entry counts. Read and write permissions derive from the owner scope.

title: Vaults
description: Store and rotate pipeline secrets without exposing values in the interface or logs.

sections.title: Scope and encryption
sections.content: A vault belongs to an allowed scope and values are encrypted at rest. Lists never display secrets in clear text and logs apply masking.

sections.title: Secrets
sections.content: Add a key, value, and optional expiration. **Copy key reference** provides pipeline syntax without copying the secret value.

sections.title: Rotation
sections.content: Rotation creates a new value for an existing key while retaining version traceability. Update dependent external systems before retiring an old value.

sections.title: Import, export, and history
sections.content: Export contains keys only, never values. Import adds or updates provided secrets. History shows versions and dates without revealing content.

title: Releases
description: Track detected versions, build evidence, deliverables, promotions, and rollbacks.

sections.title: List and detection
sections.content: Releases belong to a project and can originate from Git tags or the delivery workflow. The list shows version, status, branch, and latest activity.

sections.title: Provenance
sections.content: Detail links tag, branch, commit, pipeline, and source run. These links trace a published version back to its exact definition and code.

sections.title: Deliverables
sections.content: Linked artifacts and deliverables are listed with destination. A usable release retains access to stored bytes, not metadata alone.

sections.title: Promotion and rollback
sections.content: Promotion advances a release to the selected environment under pipeline controls. Rollback selects an earlier compatible version and runs its contract; it does not bypass environment checks.

title: Artifacts
description: Inspect pipeline deliverables, provenance, integrity, retention, and distribution.

sections.title: Details
sections.content: Detail shows name, size, creation time, checksum, and retention. Copy the checksum to verify integrity after download.

sections.title: Provenance
sections.content: Project, pipeline, run, branch, and commit link the artifact to production. Release or environment use appears in distribution.

sections.title: Download
sections.content: Download while bytes are retained and you have read permission. Metadata can remain after the file expires; the interface then reports unavailability.

sections.title: Retention and protection
sections.content: Retention and quota policies can remove older builds. Deployed, published, or release-required artifacts are protected according to storage rules.

title: Tasks
description: Track commands sent to agents, progress, results, and associated logs.

sections.title: List
sections.content: Global and contextual lists show accessible tasks with status, server, origin, and dates. Project and server views apply their filter automatically.

sections.title: Lifecycle
sections.content: A task moves through pending, assigned, running, then success, failure, or cancellation. Real-time changes remove terminal tasks from active tracking and refresh lists.

sections.title: Agent execution
sections.content: An agent claims a task compatible with its capabilities and concurrency slots. Assigned work is not automatically redistributed to prevent repeating an external effect.

sections.title: Logs
sections.content: Open or watch the task identifier in the log console. Running output streams live and persisted output remains available after completion.

title: Task logs
description: Watch one task output stream and control display of masked values.

sections.title: Select a task
sections.content: Enter the numeric identifier and select **Watch**. The console joins that task’s real-time group and displays received lines. Start watching again after changing the identifier.

sections.title: Connection and waiting
sections.content: Connected confirms the log hub link. If no line is available, the task may not have started, may produce no output, or may have ended without retained logs.

sections.title: Masking
sections.content: **Show masked** keeps secret protection. **Show unmasked** only restores data the backend permits; values permanently masked at source cannot be recovered.

sections.title: Clear
sections.content: **Clear** empties the local console only. It does not delete persisted logs or the task. This page does not offer global agent, pipeline, or level filters.

title: Alerts
description: Define server metric rules and process triggered alerts and read state.

sections.title: Rules
sections.content: A rule has a name, server, metric, threshold, sustained duration, severity, and active state. Duration prevents triggering on a short spike.

sections.title: Create and edit
sections.content: Select metric and server, set threshold and duration, then save. Disable a rule instead of deleting it when you want to preserve configuration.

sections.title: Recent alerts
sections.content: Triggers show message, severity, server, and time. The navigation count represents unread items; **Mark all read** resets it.

sections.title: Real-time
sections.content: New triggers and rule changes arrive in real time. Administrators configure optional external channels separately under Notification rules.

title: Quality and security analysis
description: Explore project posture, normalized reports, and findings produced by analysis pipelines.

sections.title: Portfolio
sections.content: Portfolio compares projects, grades, posture, scanners, and finding volume. Filter by organization, project, pipeline, branch, commit, category, or period, then search for a finding.

sections.title: Reports and provenance
sections.content: Each record retains source, tool, pipeline run, branch, and commit. Reports aggregate tests, coverage, lint, vulnerabilities, SBOM, and other configured producers.

sections.title: Finding detail
sections.content: Detail shows rule, category, file, line, symbol, excerpt, first and last occurrence, related reports, and external documentation. Occurrences show persistence across analyses.

sections.title: Decisions
sections.content: Change status with a reason and optional expiration. History keeps author, date, reason, and decision to distinguish remediation, temporary acceptance, and false positive.

sections.title: Ticket and AI assistance
sections.content: Create a ticket when integration is available. The AI prompt assembles finding context; preview, copy, or download Markdown before using it with an authorized tool.

sections.title: Pipeline gates
sections.content: Run pages show new findings, blockers, warnings, reports, and missing producers. An incomplete gate is not treated as silent success.

title: Backups
description: Schedule file or database backups, run them on demand, and regularly verify restorability.

sections.title: Policies
sections.content: A policy combines project, server, name, active state, cron expression, and retention. Select a database engine or enter file paths for the protected workload.

sections.title: Database connection
sections.content: For PostgreSQL or MySQL, configure host, port, database, user, and password. Leave password empty during edit to keep the stored encrypted value.

sections.title: Execution
sections.content: **Run now** creates a run sent to the target agent. Run history shows status, start, size, and message. State changes arrive in real time.

sections.title: Restore check
sections.content: Restore-check cron schedules a verification separate from backup. The result reports whether content can be restored; a successful backup without a recent check does not prove restorability.

sections.title: Retention and deletion
sections.content: Retention limits old run storage. Deleting a policy removes its schedule; review dependencies and storage rules before confirming.

title: Service connections
description: Centralize access settings for external services used by projects and pipelines.

sections.title: Catalog
sections.content: Search connections and inspect name, type, project, URL, and status. A connection can be global within its allowed scope or project-owned.

sections.title: Create and edit
sections.content: Choose integration type, enter URL and required credentials, then save. Sensitive values are treated as secrets and are not redisplayed in clear text.

sections.title: Test
sections.content: **Test connection** asks the backend to verify access with stored configuration. Success validates connectivity at that moment, not future remote-service permissions.

sections.title: Use and access
sections.content: Compatible pipelines and features select a connection instead of embedding credentials. Read and edit operations follow resource and project permissions.

title: AI tasks
description: Define analyses run by an authorized AI runner, manually or on schedule, and inspect results.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.content: A task has a name, project or server owner, runner profile, active state, and optional schedule. External data identifies whether execution may send context outside the platform.

sections.title: Manual and scheduled runs
sections.content: **Run now** creates a server task and waits for its result through real-time completion. A scheduled definition follows its calendar expression; a disabled definition does not start automatically.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: The page shows runs over the last seven days, failures, and duration. Open Results to inspect Markdown report, metadata, and each run status.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: The selected profile fixes binary, timeout, and external-data permission. Review outgoing content before enabling an integration that leaves your infrastructure.

title: Custom dashboards
description: Compose monitoring views with configurable widgets and select the default home view.

sections.title: List
sections.content: The list shows name, widget count, and default dashboard. Create, edit, or delete according to administrative permissions.

sections.title: Widgets
sections.content: Add a widget, select its type, and configure title, visibility, column, width, and height. Widget-specific settings determine its data source.

sections.title: Layout
sections.content: Move widgets up or down and use Preview before saving. Dimensions should remain compatible with the responsive grid.

sections.title: Default view
sections.content: Mark one dashboard as default to replace standard home content. Only one dashboard should hold this role at a time.

title: Organizations
description: Scope ownership of projects, servers, and members and manage organization-wide rules.

sections.title: Create and edit
sections.content: Set name, slug, and description. The slug identifies the organization in selectors and integrations; choose it carefully.

sections.title: Members
sections.content: Add a user with the desired role or remove one. Owner controls the organization. Membership and permission changes propagate to affected sessions.

sections.title: Projects
sections.content: Detail lists owned projects and supports assignment where available. Organization resources become visible according to member roles and effective permissions.

sections.title: Quality gates
sections.content: Shared quality settings can define expectations for organization projects. Evaluate changes against pipelines that consume these rules.

sections.title: Deletion
sections.content: Deletion is blocked or dangerous while resources depend on the organization. Reassign dependencies before confirming.

title: Roles and permissions
description: Compose rights by resource type and scope, assign roles to users, and inspect change history.

sections.title: Roles
sections.content: Create a role with name, description, and active state, or clone an existing role. A disabled role should no longer grant its permissions.

sections.title: Permission matrix
sections.content: The matrix combines resource type, scope, and Read, Write, or Admin level. Bulk actions apply a level to several rows; review before saving.

sections.title: Users
sections.content: Add or remove users from the role tab. A user can hold multiple roles and effective rights are the union of allowed grants.

sections.title: Effective access
sections.content: Organizations and direct permissions supplement roles. Changes take effect live and may show a blocking acknowledgement dialog to the affected user.

sections.title: Audit
sections.content: Audit records date, action, and author of role changes. Use it to explain permission evolution.

title: Users
description: Manage accounts, passwords, organizations, roles, TOTP, and effective permissions.

sections.title: List
sections.content: Search by username or email, filter state, and inspect roles and creation time. Active and disabled accounts are clearly distinguished.

sections.title: Create and edit
sections.content: Enter username, email, initial password, and state. **Must change password** forces renewal at the next sign-in.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: Change or reset password and inspect TOTP state. Passwords follow minimum length and are never displayed again.

sections.title: Roles and organizations
sections.content: Assign roles and add the user to allowed organizations. Removing organization membership removes the corresponding inherited access.

sections.title: Effective permissions
sections.content: The view lists resource type, permission, and origin, including granting role. Refresh after a change to verify the actual result.

sections.title: Deletion
sections.content: Deleting an account is a sensitive administrative action. Review memberships and resource ownership before confirmation.

title: Notification rules
description: Configure outbound channels and rules that turn platform events into external notifications.

sections.title: Channels
sections.content: A channel defines destination type and connection settings. Create, edit, enable, or disable channels without changing rules that reference them.

sections.title: Test a channel
sections.content: **Test connection** sends or prepares a check to the configured destination. Success confirms current settings but not future provider availability.

sections.title: Rules
sections.content: A rule has a name, event type, channel, and active state. Use separate rules when events need different destinations.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.content: When no notification arrives, check rule state, event type, channel state, connection test, then system and audit logs.

title: AI runner profiles
description: Declare allowed AI executables, timeouts, and external-data policy.

sections.title: Profiles
sections.content: Each profile has a name, binary, timeout, and external-data permission. AI tasks select a profile rather than accepting a free-form command.

sections.title: Create and edit
sections.content: Use a controlled executable installed on the runner. Match timeout to real workload without turning a stalled process into unlimited waiting.

sections.title: External data
sections.content: Enable only when the runner may transmit context outside the infrastructure. Task definitions also display this choice so the risk remains visible.

sections.title: Deletion
sections.content: Before deleting a profile, verify that no active AI task definition references it. Deletion removes the shared runner choice and cannot repair existing task definitions.

title: Package feeds
description: Reference upstream NuGet or npm sources, synchronize packages, and manage the tracked catalog.

sections.title: Create a feed
sections.content: Set name, NuGet or npm type, and upstream URL. Use a registry URL compatible with the selected type.

sections.title: Tracked packages
sections.content: **Manage packages** opens the feed catalog. Add or remove packages whose versions should be resolved and synchronized.

sections.title: Synchronization
sections.content: Synchronization queries upstream, stores supported versions, and reports failures, unsupported packages, or rate limits. The page updates when the hosted service completes a change.

sections.title: Refresh and delete
sections.content: Refresh to reread persisted state. Deleting a feed removes configuration and tracking; review catalog consumers first.

title: Package registry
description: Browse NuGet and npm packages stored in the internal registry and available versions.

sections.title: Catalog
sections.content: Search by name and inspect type, latest version, update time, size, and version count. Publication events refresh the list in real time.

sections.title: Versions
sections.content: Open a package to see every version, size, date, and available metadata. The main list identifies the latest version.

sections.title: NuGet
sections.content: The page presents the internal NuGet feed URL. Configure it in an authorized client, then use standard NuGet or `dotnet` commands with required credentials.

sections.title: npm
sections.content: The page presents the internal npm registry URL. Configure it in `.npmrc` or for the command and provide expected authentication.

sections.title: Registry and feeds
sections.content: Package feeds describe tracked upstream sources; Package registry describes packages actually stored and served by Aetheus. They are separate catalogs.

title: Plugins
description: Register and manage extensions known to the platform.

sections.title: Catalog
sections.content: Search plugins and inspect name, author, version, type, status, and creation time.

sections.title: Register
sections.content: Provide metadata and entry point expected by the plugin type. Registration does not replace installing dependencies in the runtime environment.

sections.title: Edit and unregister
sections.content: Update metadata or status when a version changes. Unregistering removes the extension; verify no active configuration depends on it.

title: Audit log
description: Search sensitive actions and verify audit-chain integrity.

sections.title: Search
sections.content: Filter by text, action, entity type, and date range. Each entry shows timestamp, user, action, entity, and identifier.

sections.title: Details
sections.content: Open an entry to inspect and copy recorded details during investigation. Secret values must not appear in audit data.

sections.title: Integrity
sections.content: **Verify chain** checks cryptographic links between entries. Results distinguish intact entries, a precise break, or unavailable verification.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.content: An intact chain proves consistency of available records, not absence of an unaudited external action. Correlate with system logs and affected resources.

title: System logs
description: Analyze backend logs with filters, correlation, export, and automatic refresh.

sections.title: Filters
sections.content: Filter by file, level, category, text, correlation identifier, and date range. Clear filters to return to the general view.

sections.title: Navigation
sections.content: Refresh manually, enable automatic refresh, or load more rows. The counter reports currently displayed entries.

sections.title: Details and correlation
sections.content: Open the complete message and copy message or correlation identifier. Search the same identifier to trace one request across components.

sections.title: Export and purge
sections.content: Download the selected file or export results as CSV. Purge is a destructive administrative action requiring confirmation and must follow retention policy.

title: API reference
description: Browse the active backend OpenAPI contract and find method, path, domain, and summary.

sections.title: Source
sections.content: The page loads the current backend OpenAPI document. It reflects endpoints published by this version rather than a copied help list.

sections.title: Navigation
sections.content: Endpoints are grouped by tag. Each row shows HTTP method, path, and summary. Search path, summary, or domain.

sections.title: Access
sections.content: Reference visibility does not bypass endpoint authentication or authorization. Integrations must use an approved authentication mechanism and follow contract validation.

sections.title: Diagnostics
sections.content: If the list is empty, verify backend availability and OpenAPI access. Incompatible frontend and backend versions can also produce an unexpected reference.

title: User settings
description: Manage profile, appearance, language, notifications, password, TOTP, and personal access tokens.

sections.title: Profile
sections.content: Change display name and inspect username, role, and account information. Username remains the sign-in identifier.

sections.title: Appearance and language
sections.content: Choose light or dark theme and French or English. Theme persists in the browser; language reloads resources and the matching help catalog.

sections.title: Notification preferences
sections.content: Enable or disable email, pipeline, and server alerts for your account. These preferences differ from global channels and rules managed by administrators.

sections.title: Password
sections.content: Enter current password, new password, and confirmation. An account marked **Must change password** is sent to the required flow after sign-in.

sections.title: Two-factor authentication
sections.content: Enable TOTP by scanning the QR code or using the manual key, then verify a code. Store recovery codes outside the application. Disabling requires confirmation.

sections.title: Personal access tokens
sections.content: Create a token with name, scope, and expiration. The complete value appears once: copy it immediately into a secret manager. The list shows prefix, state, creation, expiration, and last use; revoke any compromised token.

sections.title: About
sections.content: About shows the application version and general product information. Include the displayed version when reporting a problem so support can identify the exact build.

title: Platform settings
description: Manage shared secrets, registration tokens, and platform quality gates.

sections.title: General
sections.content: General settings control global behaviors exposed by this version. Save each group after change and verify consuming components.

sections.title: Secrets
sections.content: Add or update a shared secret key. Values are protected and can be shown temporarily according to permissions. Deleting a secret can break an integration; identify consumers first.

sections.title: Registration tokens
sections.content: Generate a token to enroll an agent, copy it while available, and monitor expiration and use. Revoke unused or exposed tokens.

sections.title: Quality gates
sections.content: Configure global thresholds proposed to analyses and pipelines. More specific rules can supplement or replace them according to scope.

title: Administration
description: Entry point for platform administrator features.

sections.title: Identity and access
sections.content: Users, Organizations, and Roles manage accounts, membership, resource ownership, and effective permissions.

sections.title: Monitoring and compliance
sections.content: Audit log verifies actions and chain integrity. System logs supports diagnostics. Dashboards configures the shared home view.

sections.title: Integrations
sections.content: Notification rules, AI runner profiles, Package feeds, Package registry, and Plugins configure cross-platform services.

sections.title: Platform and API
sections.content: Platform settings contains secrets, registration tokens, and quality gates. API reference exposes the active backend OpenAPI contract.

sections.title: Access control
sections.content: The Administration menu is visible only to administrators. Each screen applies its own checks and confirmations; help grants no additional rights.
